sections_target.text: Introduction
The device provides protection against earth leakage.

This document was prepared by North Delta Electricity Distribution Company and discussed at the meeting of the MPIS coordinators of the distribution companies on / / and the document was approved for implementation.
Safety Precautions
Issue an approved work order; maintenance personnel must carry the occupational safety and health category card.
Ensure warning signs are posted (Under Test).
Occupational safety and health instructions must be followed at the work site.
Switch off the circuit breaker and place it in the test position outside the cell.
Do not open current transformers while in service or during testing.
Do not short-circuit the secondary winding terminals of the voltage transformers of the installed protection device.
Earth the protection device to protect it.

Observe polarity when dealing with DC voltage.
DC Voltage
Switch off the DC circuit breakers when dealing with their circuits.

Observe occupational safety and health instructions when handling batteries (wear gloves, safety goggles, avometer, fork for measuring battery voltage, hydrometer for measuring battery solution density).

sections_target.text: Procedures to be Carried Out

All tests is done according to IEC 60255-5 ANSI / 
IEEEC 37.90.0

Frequency of 
Testing

It is a visual inspection of the relay cover can reveal valuable information. Recommended that protective and auxiliary relays be given a complete calibration test and inspection at least once a year. This schedule however sometimes cannot be met due to existing workloads and available manpower with the result that routine calibration tests intervals of many relays are longer than a year.
Test Records

A complete record should be kept of all test data and observations made during tests and inspections including identifying numbers of test equipment used. The following relay test report forms are available at distribution points.
Visual Inspection of the Device

A visual inspection of the relay cover can reveal valuable information. Any excessive dust, dirt or metallic material deposited on the cover should be noted and removed thus preventing such material from entering the relay when the cover is removed. A cover glass which is fogged should be cleaned fogging is in most cases a normal condition due to volatile materials being driven out of coils and insulating materials, and is not an indication of a problem.

Procedures to be Carried Out
All tests is done according to IEC 60255-5 ANSI / 
IEEEC 37.90.0
Frequency of 
Testing
It is a visual inspection of the relay cover can reveal valuable information. Recommended that protective and auxiliary relays be given a complete calibration test and inspection at least once a year. This schedule however sometimes cannot be met due to existing workloads and available manpower with the result that routine calibration tests intervals of many relays are longer than a year.
Test Records
A complete record should be kept of all test data and observations made during tests and inspections including identifying numbers of test equipment used. The following relay test report forms are available at distribution points.
Visual Inspection of the Device
A visual inspection of the relay cover can reveal valuable information. Any excessive dust, dirt or metallic material deposited on the cover should be noted and removed thus preventing such material from entering the relay when the cover is removed. A cover glass which is fogged should be cleaned fogging is in most cases a normal condition due to volatile materials being driven out of coils and insulating materials, and is not an indication of a problem.
Connect the current leads (injection device output) to the protection device terminal block at points 1 and 2, which are the earth current points IE | 1.
Raise the current value gradually until reaching the pickup value set on the device | 2.
Record this value in the Test Sheet | 3.
Lower the current to reach I Reset, then calculate the Reset Factor from Reset current / Pickup current | 4.
Connect the Trip leads of the protection device, points 3 and 4, to the timer points on the injection device | 5.
If a correct time grading is required, the circuit breaker time shall be taken into account; the circuit breaker of this cell shall then be connected, with the two timer leads connected to the circuit breaker terminals, and the tripping time calculated for each phase | 6.
Inject the protection device with the pickup value and record the tripping time, which represents the tripping time of the relay only; repeat with the circuit breaker to determine the mechanical tripping time of the circuit breaker | 7.
